items.title: Postgres 19 is late because so many more bugs are being found now
items.author: soheilpro
items.summary: According to Robert Haas, PostgreSQL 19 is delayed because more bugs are being found now, which takes more time to fix. He explains that LLMs can draft fixes, but they aren’t always correct or compliant with PostgreSQL standards, so they still need to be reviewed and committed by humans. The number of commits back-patched to prior releases jumped by more than 74% in a single year, indicating a surge in bug reports from AI/LLM agents.

items.title: New 3D thermal invisibility cloak makes objects disappear from infrared cameras
items.author: stevenalowe
items.summary: Researchers from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign have developed a groundbreaking 3D invisibility cloak that can hide complex objects from infrared cameras while protecting them from extreme heat and cold. Instead of blocking heat, the device guides it around an object, making the object appear invisible to thermal imaging from virtually any direction. Successfully built and tested, the cloak could transform electronics cooling, thermal protection, and stealth technology.

items.title: Keeping Up Appearances – The women taking over the funeral industry
items.author: TMWNN
items.summary: The sources indicate that three women, Lucy, Jane, and Jordana, are working in different sectors of the deathcare industry and aim to bring care where they found neglect. The funeral industry professionalized after the Civil War with embalming, transitioning from domestic labor performed by women to professional practices. The article from the Los Angeles Review of Books highlights these women's efforts to address this shift and bring a more caring approach to the industry. The Wikipedia entry on "Keeping Up Appearances" is unrelated to the topic of women in the funeral industry.

items.title: AI fan wikis riddled with errors are muddying the waters of games culture
items.author: rdmuser
items.summary: Eurogamer has highlighted that AI fan wikis riddled with errors are complicating an already contested part of games culture. The tools have made it easy for bad actors to crowd out good information, muddying the waters of an already contested part of games culture. Independent groups creating these wikis struggle to compete with larger hosting sites like Fandom, which have also had to roll back AI features due to inaccuracies. The presence of these erroneous AI-generated wikis has hurt the reputation of legitimate volunteer-led resources.

items.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks
items.author: luu
items.summary: According to the sources, the AI cost of JavaScript frameworks includes the following figures: Gracile+Lit at $4.65 (3.92–5.07), Angular at $4.97 (3.19–6.82), and React Router at 12.5 min (8.4–13.6). The sources also mention that Angular has a cost of 9.76 M (4.92–14.94). However, the sources do not provide a definitive answer on the AI cost of all JavaScript frameworks.

items.title: Radiation Map of the World
items.author: slater
items.summary: The sources provide information about global radiation maps. Radiaverse features a global radiation map measured by its users, with 45,821,260 dose-rate points from 18,458 tracks covering 950 areas. The Geiger Counter World Map offers real-time radiation and radon levels globally, categorized by CPM and pCi/L. The Pinterest pin discusses a global solar irradiation map, showing potential solar energy variation worldwide. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the specific question about the current radiation map of the world.

items.title: Novellas with Groff
items.author: dverlaeckt80
items.summary: Lauren Groff has authored five novels, including THE VASTER WILDS, MATRIX, FATES AND FURIES, ARCADIA, and THE MONSTERS OF TEMPLETON. Her story collections include FLORIDA and DELICATE EDIBLE BIRDS. The sources do not provide information on novellas written by Groff.

items.title: Seoul Viosys begins production of rare-earth-free white light emitter
items.author: gmays
items.summary: Seoul Viosys Co., Ltd. has begun mass production of a rare-earth-free white light emitter, specifically the WICOP 3 chip, which can be as small as 10 micrometers. This innovation eliminates the need for rare earth materials like yttrium aluminum garnet (YAG) traditionally used in white LEDs. The company expects this to create a new market significantly larger than the current $10bn white LED market. However, claims about the manufacturing cost, reliability, and color efficacy of the new technology still await independent validation.

items.title: Domain hacks with unusual Unicode characters (2018)
items.author: n_plus_1_acc
items.summary: The sources mention domain hacks using unusual Unicode characters, specifically listing various symbols and their associated countries or regions, such as `㏕` for the US Military, `℡` for .tel registry, `№` for Norway, `㍳` for Australia, `㎞` & `㏎` for Comoros, and `㎺` for Palau. Terence Eden's blog post details these hacks extensively, showing how Unicode symbols are creatively used in domain names. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to any specific question about these domain hacks beyond the listed examples.

items.title: Frontier Airlines Likely Breached
items.summary: Frontier Airlines disclosed a data breach on or about July 9, 2026, which may have exposed certain personal information, including Social Security numbers. The breach was reported to the Vermont Attorney General, and Frontier Airlines initiated incident response protocols, notified law enforcement, and engaged a third-party cybersecurity firm for investigation. The breach was also claimed by a group called ExfilSquad, which listed Frontier Airlines among its victims in a data extortion campaign on July 26, 2026. The exact nature and scope of the breach remain undisclosed.

items.title: The Megadonors Who Have Poured $1.2B into the Midterms
items.author: doener
items.summary: The 2026 US midterms have seen significant financial contributions from megadonors, with $1.2 billion poured into the elections, according to The New York Times. The top Republican donors include Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz ($115.3 million), Elon Musk ($90.5 million), and Greg and Anna Brockman ($50 million). On the Democratic side, George and Alex Soros ($103.7 million) and Jeff Yass ($93.8 million) are among the major contributors. The rising influence of tech industry donors, predominantly Republican, reflects the party's advantage in midterm funding.

items.title: Leaking Secrets from Air-Gap Computers by Spelling Radio Signals from RAM (2024)
items.author: hapax_legomena
items.summary: The paper "RAMBO: Leaking Secrets from Air-Gap Computers by Spelling Covert Radio Signals from Computer RAM" presents a novel technique for exfiltrating data from air-gapped computers by emitting electromagnetic radiation (EMR) from RAM modules. Led by Mordechai Guri from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, the authors analyze the practical feasibility and countermeasures of this covert channel. LinkedIn posts by Graftholders and Rojesh M. Shikhrakar echo the paper's findings, emphasizing the ability to extract data from air-gapped systems through malware-induced radio signals. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to specific questions about implementation details or exact countermeasures.

items.title: Understanding Email Encryption (2025)
items.author: nmjenkins
items.summary: The global email encryption market is projected to grow from USD 9.30 billion in 2025 to USD 23.33 billion by 2030 at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 20.2%. This growth is driven by rising email data breaches, increased BEC frauds, spear phishing, and stringent data privacy regulations. The Asia Pacific region is witnessing the fastest growth due to rapid digital transformation and a sharp increase in cyber threats. The market's growth is also propelled by regulatory compliance requirements and the expansion of remote work and mobile workforces.

items.title: I Am the Reason OpenAI Is Killing Unlimited Chats
items.author: gulmothrowaway
items.summary: According to the sources, an AI developer has built a custom multi-agent coding workflow using local Model Context Protocol servers and OpenAI's Secure MCP Tunnel connected to ChatGPT. This developer could execute development work without hitting Codex limits by orchestrating tasks via GitHub issues and parallel chat sessions. Following OpenAI's decision to eliminate unlimited chats, the developer plans to transition to using Claude models. However, the sources do not definitively state that this developer is the reason for the change. Additionally, PCWorld reports that free users of ChatGPT are now getting unlimited text chats and a new default model in GPT-5.6 Luna.

items.title: Memdoor: A team of 5 Qwen3.8-27B models beats Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
items.author: guregodevo
items.summary: Memdoor's team-solve example runs five Qwen3.8-27B instances as a planner, two parallel ideators, a solver and a manager, with a repair worker on top, and scored a mean 9.8 of 10 over five passes on the first ten LiveCodeBench Hard problems. This beats the 8.0 that Fable 5 posts on the same ten alone, and edges past the 9.6 of the GVS5H harness by Lee (2026) that it reproduces. The agents never share a chat context.

items.title: In LLM era, can software startup survive?
items.author: sjia
items.text:
Nowadays, vibe coding is everywhere. Turning an idea into software is just matter of tokens. I was joking the other day. Creating a tax return softwar is much faster than purchasing Turbotax at Costco.

Large companies still have compute resources and customer bases. For startup, users are expecting open source and free software. Posts of subscription or one-time purchase software on Reddit will get tons of downvotes instantly.
items.summary: In the LLM era, software startups face challenges as the cost of development becomes cheap but lacks a moat, and distribution channels are hard for small businesses. According to LinkedIn, the traditional high profit margins in software businesses are no longer feasible due to high operational costs, similar to a restaurant business. Foundation Capital notes that startups that were AI-native and embedded LLMs into user workflows found themselves in a precarious position as model providers launched their own apps and changed API terms, building competing products. The sources suggest that startups need to settle distribution channels, productize solutions, or convert to a service model to survive.

items.title: AI agent swarms in Minecraft fail to build civilization, drown in bureaucracy
items.author: entryleveljobsc
items.summary: Researchers unleashed AI agent swarms in Minecraft to build a thriving civilization, but the fifty-agent teams fell into paralyzing bureaucracy. The agents spent more time in meetings and status updates than building, creating elaborate governance structures that consumed all their resources. After zombies killed many agents on the first night, ambitious initial tasks were abandoned, and the colony fell into bureaucracy, with four agents spending 11 minutes appointing a 'sole fertilizer operator' for a single piece of bone meal on one wheat block.
